report.state_of_the_book:
At the close of 1 July 2026 the book holds 60 episodes. Fifteen are closed, carrying $192,874.63 expected and $200,968.01 received [[overview:by_disposition.CLOSED]]. Thirty-four sit in exception, with $749,716.90 expected against $443,203.53 received and $424,387.21 of absolute variance; 26 of those are episodes that had closed and came undone [[overview:by_disposition.EXCEPTION]]. Eleven are pending $133,600.42 against $56,699.24, a $76,901.18 variance [[overview:by_disposition.PENDING]].

The exception book is the whole story: it holds the large majority of the money and nearly all the reworked episodes. The reason codes cited most often are an awaiting remittance, a denial, no cash, and a rejected rebate, four episodes each [[overview:reason_codes]]. Cross-track flags are sparse — the largest, X-1 and X-2, touch three episodes apiece [[overview:cross_track_flags]].
report.what_is_concentrated:
Sorted by absolute dollars at variance, two denied medical episodes lead: E-000006 at $84,240.00 and E-000052 at $84,240.00, both denied with no appeal filed and the first reopened from pending [[queue:E-000006]] [[queue:E-000052]]. E-000032 follows at $37,373.75, a pharmacy episode whose remittance claims payment but the bank shows no matching deposit [[queue:E-000032]], then E-000047 at -$32,436.00, a duplicate remittance that had been closed and came back [[queue:E-000047]], and E-000040 at $24,334.91, which carries both a missing payer payment and a missing rebate payment [[queue:E-000040]].

Sorted by age, the longest-standing exception is E-000001 at 358 days, an unexplained adjustment residual [[queue:E-000001]]; next E-000006 at 336 days [[queue:E-000006]], then E-000007 at 324 days with an approved rebate and no cash [[queue:E-000007]].

Sorted to put reopened episodes first, the leaders are E-000022 and E-000019, both clawed-back rebates reopened from closed [[queue:E-000022]] [[queue:E-000019]], followed by E-000027, a duplicate payment reopened from closed at -$6,638.63 [[queue:E-000027]], and E-000030, reopened from closed on a cash mismatch [[queue:E-000030]].
report.what_i_could_not_determine: Two episodes carry an insufficient-data reason code [[overview:reason_codes]], so their reconciliation is incomplete on the face of the record; E-000040 and E-000014 carry that code at the episode level, and both also carry a correlated cash gap or an untraceable recoupment [[queue:E-000040]] [[queue:E-000014]]. Whether unallocated bank deposits belong to the no-cash episodes requires get_cash_match, which I did not call.
report.where_to_look_first: The two $84,240.00 denials, E-000006 and E-000052, surfaced by the queue sorted by absolute variance [[queue:E-000006]] [[queue:E-000052]]. The no-cash episodes at the top of that same sort, E-000032 and E-000040, where the payer's remittance and the bank disagree [[queue:E-000032]] [[queue:E-000040]]. And the four episodes reopened from closed — E-000022, E-000019, E-000027, E-000030 — surfaced by the queue sorted to put reopened episodes first [[queue:E-000022]] [[queue:E-000019]] [[queue:E-000027]] [[queue:E-000030]].
